inline_comments.comment: Changing `getConfig()?.htmlLabels` to `getConfig()?.flowchart?.htmlLabels` is a silent behavioral regression. The original expression accessed a non-existent top-level `htmlLabels` property, which returned `undefined` and made `evaluate(undefined)` resolve to `false` — effectively making `node.useHtmlLabels` the sole enabler. Now `getConfig()?.flowchart?.htmlLabels` returns `true` (the flowchart default), so every diagram using this `labelHelper` will have HTML labels **force-enabled** by default. Worse, the `||` operator means that even a node that explicitly sets `useHtmlLabels = false` (evaluates to `false`) will have the right-hand side evaluated, and `true` will win. Non-flowchart diagrams that deliberately opted out of HTML labels will be silently switched over. If the goal is to read `htmlLabels` from config, this should use the diagram-specific config path or stay gated behind `node.useHtmlLabels`.

`applyStyle(span, node.labelStyle)` and `applyStyle(div, node.labelStyle)` on lines 55 and 58 both write the same `style` attribute to the `<span>` and its parent `<div>`. The original code only applied the style to the outer `div`. Inherited CSS properties like `font-size`, `color`, and `font-weight` will now be set on both elements, meaning they may appear on the span twice through direct assignment and CSS inheritance simultaneously. This can cause unintended visual differences — for example, a `font-size` value that is compounded through nesting. The span only needs the class assignment (`span.attr('class', labelClass)`); the style should remain on the div only.

The 5th argument passed to `createLabel` for all four terminal edge labels (start/end, left/right) is `useHtmlLabels`, but the 5th parameter in `createLabel`'s new signature is `addBackground`. These mean completely different things. `addBackground` controls whether `div.attr('class', 'labelBkg')` is applied — i.e., it's a visual styling flag. `useHtmlLabels` indicates whether HTML rendering is active. The result is that when `htmlLabels` is enabled, every terminal edge label now gets the `labelBkg` CSS background class applied, which was not the previous behavior. If the intent is to add a background to terminal labels only when using HTML mode, that should be explicitly documented and named. If not, this should be `false`.

`getConfig()` is called twice in rapid succession on lines 26–27 inside `setupImage()` — once for the truthiness check and once for the actual value. Per the project's established convention, `getConfig()` should only be called once per function and the result cached in a local variable:
```ts
const config = getConfig();
const bodyFontSize = config.fontSize
  ? config.fontSize
  : window.getComputedStyle(document.body).fontSize;
```
This is especially relevant here because `setupImage` runs once per image element inside a `Promise.all`, so `getConfig()` is being invoked multiple times per label render.

`edge.width || getConfig().flowchart?.wrappingWidth` uses logical OR (`||`), which will fall through to the config value if `edge.width` is `0` (a potentially valid falsy number). Prefer the nullish coalescing operator (`??`) so that only `null` and `undefined` trigger the fallback, consistent with how `width ?? getWrappingWidth()` is used in `addHtmlLabel`:
```js
const width = edge.width ?? getConfig().flowchart?.wrappingWidth;
```

The original `addHtmlLabel` included `div.style('padding-right', '1px')` with an explicit `// Fix for firefox` comment. This style has been silently removed with no explanation or replacement. If the Firefox rendering issue that necessitated this workaround has been resolved (e.g., by a browser update or by the new DOM measurement approach), that should be documented in a comment. If it's still needed, removing it is a regression.

The JSDoc block on lines 10–17 describes the `configureLabelImages` function — but that function was moved into `labelImageUtils.ts`. This JSDoc is now a free-floating comment attached to nothing in `util.ts`. It should either be removed or moved to the function definition in `labelImageUtils.ts` where it actually belongs.

The bump type is `patch`, but the PR description explicitly states that labels now gain **KaTeX support** and **FontAwesome iconpack support** that were previously unavailable. These are new user-facing features, not just bug fixes. Per the project's changeset conventions, feature additions should use `minor`. Using `patch` for a feature bump will result in an incorrect version increment and misleading CHANGELOG entries.

general_comments.comment: No unit tests are added for the new `configureLabelImages` utility in `labelImageUtils.ts`. Per project conventions, new utility functions should have dedicated unit tests covering at least: a container with no images (early return path), a container with images and accompanying text (`img.style.width = '100%'` path), and a container with only images (the default-width/font-size path). The current PR relies entirely on implicit integration coverage through existing Cypress snapshot tests, making it difficult to detect regressions in the new module in isolation.

In `addHtmlLabel` (`createLabel.js`), the `foreignObject` is given initial dimensions of `width: 10000, height: 10000` while attached to the hidden temp SVG for measurement. This is a common pattern but means that if any browser extension, accessibility tool, or test environment observes the DOM during this window, it sees an enormous invisible SVG element. A smaller sentinel value like `1` (or omitting the dimensions until after measurement) would be less surprising and more consistent with how other measurement utilities in the project work.
